subject: Forensic access & sampling bands — MSA security exhibit coordination
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mark Evans <mark.evans@bluecare.io>, Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Forensic access & sampling bands — MSA security exhibit coordination

Hi Mark / Alice —

Thanks for sending over the latest MSA + Order Form. I reviewed the security exhibit draft and attached a focused redline (security-exhibit-draft-20260830.docx) that aims to address two things BlueCare raised in the kickoff: (1) clarity on pen test access windows and notice, and (2) an operational pattern for evidence delivery that doesn't require ad hoc exports during every review.

High-level summary of the proposed changes: 
- Forensic access: we propose a read-only, timeboxed forensic snapshot option (48-72 hrs) for critical incidents with a written request + SOC2/Legal confirmation. This is scoped to logs/metadata + exported artifacts; we explicitly exclude bulk customer content extraction unless compelled by legal process.
- Sampling bands: instead of continuous full-scan evidence delivery, we suggest a sampling-band model (monthly rolling samples per service boundary) plus a 2-week windows for targeted evidence requested in a security review.
- Pen test language: maintain a 14-day notice for scheduled penetration tests with a 48-hour short-notice carve for emergency proofs; we also added a staging-access checklist to minimize blast radius.
- SOC 2: we confirm Redwood will share the most recent SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and keep an evergreen timeframe for annual attestations.

Attachment: security-exhibit-draft-20260830.docx (redlines inline).

Next steps I’m proposing: 
1) BlueCare legal to comment on the forensic access boundaries and confirm whether read-only snapshots are acceptable.
2) If agreed, Laura (cc'd) will fold the redline into the MSA and update the Order Form references.
3) Ben to propose a cadence for evidence delivery (samples + ad-hoc windows) and map to our observability retention.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call today if useful — I can do 11:30–12:30 PT.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Mark Evans <mark.evans@bluecare.io>

Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@heliumhealth.com>, BlueCare Legal <legal@bluecare.io>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Forensic access & sampling bands — MSA security exhibit coordination

Jordan —

Thanks for the concise redline. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before routing to legal: 
1) Forensic snapshot scope — can you confirm the exact artifacts included (e.g., request logs, console events, persisted prompt/response pairs)? We need to ensure PHI/PII handling is explicit.
2) Sampling bands — what percentage of traffic / time window would you define as the standard monthly sample? We need to size the work for our auditors.
3) Pen test notice — 14 days is fine for scheduled tests, but BlueCare requires a maximum of two short-notice tests per year; can Redwood accommodate that with the staging checklist?

If it helps, Alice and I can take a quick read-through with our security ops and circle back with specific redline suggestions by Wednesday. Also, please confirm whether the SOC2 report you reference includes the latest network segmentation controls (we requested that in the initial RFI).

Best,
Mark Evans
Head of Procurement | BlueCare Health
mark.evans@bluecare.io
+1 (617) 222-3344
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mark Evans <mark.evans@bluecare.io>, Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Forensic access & sampling bands — MSA security exhibit coordination

Mark / Alice —

Answers inline to your questions: 

1) Forensic snapshot scope: 
- Included: request/ingest logs (timestamp, request id, headers), system console events, error traces, model inference metadata (model id, truncated prompt hashes), orchestration logs, and ephemeral KV cache metadata.
- Excluded: full prompt/response payloads containing customer data unless BlueCare signs the narrow data-access consent clause (we added this as a separate opt-in paragraph).
- PII/PHI note: we will only provide artifacts that do not expose raw PHI. If a reviewer needs deeper access, we require a written justification and an agreed tight window under the forensic access process.

2) Sampling bands: 
- Default: 1% traffic monthly rolling sample per major service boundary (ingest, inference, storage) with sample artifacts retained for 30 days in an auditor-accessible view.
- Targeted windows: 14-day evidence window on request (two requests per rolling 12 months without additional charge). Extra ad-hoc windows are billable per SOW.

3) Pen test notice: we can accommodate up to two short-notice (<=48h) tests per year under the staging checklist and a guardrail that limits attack surface to non-production or limited-scope environments.

SOC2: Confirmed — our latest SOC 2 Type II (covering network segmentation controls called out in section 4.2) is available under NDA. I’ve attached the DocuSign link and Drive folder below.

Action items I’ll take on: 
- Laura will craft the opt-in paragraph for deeper data extracts and fold the sampling bands into the exhibit.
- Ben will outline a proposed calendar for monthly sample exports and the auditor-access view. 
- Jordan to schedule a 30-min alignment call with BlueCare security ops on Wed 09/02 10:00 PT (tentative).

If that works, please confirm meeting and we’ll send calendar invite.

Thanks — Jordan
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mark Evans <mark.evans@bluecare.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Forensic access & sampling bands — MSA security exhibit coordination

Mark / Jordan / Alice —

Quick operational note following our internal runbook review: 

- Monthly sample mechanics: we will export a sampling manifest (IDs + non-sensitive metadata) and a time-limited auditor view in the Drive folder. Proposed default: 1% monthly sample, pulled on the 1st of each month, retained in the auditor view for 30 days; we’ll provide a checksum manifest to validate exports.
- Evidence cadence: two scheduled monthly samples + one 14-day targeted window on request are included in the base order form. Additional windows (beyond two per 12 months or larger extraction sizes) will be scoped via SOW with estimated effort.
- Forensic snapshot runbook summary: request via security portal -> Redwood triage (48h) -> timeboxed snapshot (48–72h) -> reviewer access via pre-provisioned role. We will not provide direct DB dumps; this is a controlled read-only export.

Attachments: MSA-redline-v3.docx, OrderForm-BlueCare-v2.pdf (updated references to sampling bands).

Next steps: Laura and I will incorporate these mechanics into the MSA redline this afternoon. Laura, when can you provide a legal-ready redline for BlueCare Legal to review? Mark / Alice, if you confirm the short-notice two-test allowance and the 1% sampling band, we’ll mark these as agreed points for your procurement queue.

Ben Carter
Manager, Solutions Ops | Redwood Inference
